title: READ-Bench: Benchmarking Historical Instance Retrieval for Time-Series Diagnosis
abstract: arXiv:2609.32123v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Time-series diagnostic systems rarely rely on retrieving relevant historical cases, and when they do, retrieval is evaluated only indirectly through downstream prediction. We introduce READ-Bench, a benchmark for historical-case retrieval across 12 diagnostic datasets, centered on multivariate time series, that defines relevance by shared fault or event type rather than signal shape, so visually different traces of the same fault count as relevant while similar-looking traces of different faults do not. Treating retrieval as a base retriever followed by a reranker, we evaluate classical distances, symbolic retrievers, self-supervised and foundation-model embedders, and their fusion, plus label-aware and language-model rerankers, under one protocol that varies supervision, pollution, and corpus scale with significance testing. translated_title: READ-Bench：面向时间序列诊断的历史实例检索基准测试
translated_abstract: 时间序列诊断系统很少依赖检索相关的历史案例，即使有，也仅通过下游预测间接评估检索效果。我们提出了READ-Bench，这是一个涵盖12个诊断数据集、以多元时间序列为核心的历史案例检索基准，它以共享的故障或事件类型而非信号形状来定义相关性，因此同一故障在视觉上不同的轨迹被视为相关，而不同故障但外观相似的轨迹则不相关。我们将检索建模为基础检索器后接重排序器的两阶段流程，并在统一协议下评估了经典距离度量、符号检索器、自监督与基础模型嵌入器及其融合方法，以及标签感知和语言模型重排序器，该协议通过显著性检验改变监督程度、污染程度和语料库规模。在通用的通道独立接口下，预训练表示未表现出统计学上可检测的优势（摘要原文在此处被截断）。
tldr: 提出READ-Bench基准，以共享故障类型而非信号形状定义相关性，在12个数据集上系统评估多元时间序列历史案例检索中的各类检索器与重排序器，发现预训练表示相比简单方法并无显著优势。
en_tdlr: READ-Bench establishes a benchmark for historical-case retrieval in multivariate time-series diagnosis that defines relevance by shared fault type rather than signal shape, systematically evaluating retrievers and rerankers across 12 datasets and finding that pretrained representations offer no statistically significant advantage.
